articles.title: CS reviews rollout of water transport, PM E-DRIVE initiatives in J&K
articles.description: Chief Secretary, Atal Dulloo, today reviewed the status and implementation of the introduction of inland water transport on the rivers Jhelum and Chenab, besides the rollout of electric mobility infrastructure under the Government of India’s PM E-DRIVE scheme in J&K. The meeting besides ACS, PWD was attended by Secretary, Transport; Divisional Commissioner, Jammu/Kashmir; VC, LCMA; Representative from IWAI and other concerned officers. Reviewing the progress, the Chief Secretary stressed the need for time-bound completion of all enabling infrastructure, including terminals, access facilities, navigation arrangements and removal of obstructions in terms of utility shifting, so that water transport can be operationalised within the set deadline. During the meeting, the Chief Secretary was apprised of the progress being made for developing inland water transport facilities along identified stretches of the River Jhelum (NW-49), River Chenab (NW-26) and River Ravi (NW-84). On this occasion the Secretary Transport, Avny Lavasa apprised the meeting that in River Jhelum, a 106-km cruise corridor from Sangam to Gund Prang has been identified for development. Land for 11 terminal locations has been identified at strategic points including Marham (Sangam), Pantha Chowk, Zero Bridge, Amira Kadal, Chattabal, Sumbal and Gund Prang, among others. She further divulged that removal of local coffer dams is a key requirement for ensuring uninterrupted navigation along the Jhelum stretch. The Public Works Department (PWD) has been tasked with removal of 52 such structures, of which 18 have already been cleared. On the Chenab, a 9-km stretch between Reasi and Akhnoor Fort has been identified for cruise-based water transport, while a 15-km stretch of the River Ravi at Sohar in Jammu is also being developed for the purpose. The meeting was further informed that the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) has awarded the tender for procurement of 10 specially designed hybrid eco-vessels, each having a passenger capacity of 20 persons. The vessels are scheduled for delivery by March 2027. Later the Chief Secretary also reviewed the implementation of the PM E-DRIVE Scheme in J&K, under which the administration is working towards establishing a robust charging ecosystem to support the transition to electric mobility. The meeting was informed that 50 locations across J&K have been identified and found technically feasible for installation of public EV charging stations. These include 17 sites in Jammu, 5 in Kathua, 4 in Rajouri, 3 in Udhampur, 4 in Doda, 2 each in Ramban and Reasi, and 1 in Samba. Similarly in Kashmir Division, the identified sites include 4 in Srinagar, 3 in Baramulla and 1 each in Anantnag, Budgam, Ganderbal, Pulwama and Kupwara. The Chief Secretary was also apprised of the proposal for procurement of 200 electric buses under the Gross Cost Contract (GCC) model. The proposal has received in-principle approval at the Government of India level and is being taken forward for procurement through Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL). The Chief Secretary directed all concerned departments and agencies to work in close coordination to ensure that the charging infrastructure, electrical connectivity, land requirements and other supporting facilities are put in place well ahead of the deployment of electric buses. Emphasising the importance of integrating both initiatives with J&K’s broader tourism, urban mobility and environmental sustainability goals, the Chief Secretary directed the concerned departments to maintain strict timelines and continuous monitoring at every stage. He stressed that the initiatives should translate into visible, sustainable and people-centric transport solutions, with the water transport projects and electric mobility infrastructure being progressed in a coordinated manner towards the targeted implementation within the stipulated timeframe.

articles.title: MSMEs Can Strengthen Bundelkhand’s Economy, Expand Employment Beyond Agriculture: Jhansi Commissioner
articles.description: MSMEs Can Strengthen Bundelkhand’s Economy, Expand Employment Beyond Agriculture: Jhansi Commissioner Lucknow, Sept 3 (KNN) The MSME sector has significant potential to generate employment after agriculture and strengthen local economies, Jhansi Divisional Commissioner Bimal Kumar Dubey said while inaugurating a two-day vendor development programme for MSMEs on Wednesday. Organised by the MSME Development Office, Kanpur, under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, in association with the Bundelkhand Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI), the programme featured over 15 stalls by PSUs, government departments, banks and MSME units showcasing products and services. Focus On Local Manufacturing And Procurement Dubey stressed the need to promote ‘Vocal for Local’ and highlighted MSMEs’ role in expanding employment beyond agriculture, reported Times Of India. He said public procurement policy mandates Central PSUs and government organisations to source 25 percent of annual procurement from micro and small enterprises, including sub-targets for SC/ST and women-owned businesses. He also highlighted Bundelkhand’s renewable energy potential, noting that solar power generation has reached 275 MW, with 250 MW in Jhansi and 200 MW in Lalitpur, according to figures cited at the event. Jhansi Eyeing Industrial Hub Status District Magistrate Gaurang Rathi said vendor development programmes help bridge the gap between MSMEs and markets. He said a roadmap has been prepared to develop Jhansi as an industrial hub, with making Bundelkhand a manufacturing hub among the government’s priorities. BIDA Additional CEO Praveen Verma briefed participants on public procurement provisions and GeM registration. He said a new industrial city is being developed near Jhansi, with 28,000 acres of land acquired. Jhansi Development Authority Vice-Chairman Himanshu Gautam said the authority was supporting the Defence Corridor and other industrial initiatives. A 1,200-acre housing project has also been proposed to support industrial development and MSME units. Programme To Strengthen MSME-Market Linkages BCCI President Dhiraj Khullar said the programme would benefit entrepreneurs across Bundelkhand and support the vision of a self-reliant India. MSME Development Office Director Vishnu Kumar Verma said the programme aims to facilitate direct interaction between MSMEs, government departments and PSUs, helping entrepreneurs access procurement and market opportunities. (KNN Bureau)
